questions.question: Select the appropriate option to fill in the blank. I haven't seen him _______ last week.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I haven't seen him _______ last week.
questions.solution: 'Since' is correct because it refers to a specific point of time, like 'last week.' The sentence indicates the speaker hasn’t seen the person from a specific point in time, and 'since' appropriately connects this idea. 'To' is used for direction or movement, which is incorrect in this context. 'For' indicates a duration, but the sentence uses a point of time, not a period. 'Beyond' means "further than" or "outside the limits," which is neither grammatically nor contextually correct here.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. They was / celebrating their / Silver wedding anniversary / next month in Dubai
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

They was / celebrating their / Silver wedding anniversary / next month in Dubai

options.html: next month in Dubai

questions.solution: "They was" contains the grammatical error The subject "They" is plural, so the verb must agree with it. The correct verb form is "were," not "was," because "was" is singular and does not match the plural subject "They." Corrected Sentence: "They were celebrating their Silver wedding anniversary next month in Dubai."

questions.question: The given sentence has an error. Select the option that rectifies the error. The students were asked to turn up their assignments by Friday
questions.questionHtml:
The given sentence has an error. Select the option that rectifies the error.

The students were asked to turn up their assignments by Friday

options.html: their assignment by Friday
turn in their assignments
the students asked to
asked turn up their assignments

questions.solution: The correct phrase is "turn in," which means "to submit." The correct sentence will be: "The students were asked to turn in their assignments by Friday." The phrase "turn up" is incorrect here. It means "to appear" or "to arrive," which is not contextually appropriate.
